newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-ITAU HELPED BY DROP IN DEFAULTS.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-ITAU HELPED BY DROP IN DEFAULTS.

text.p: Brazil's Banco Itau posted a 24.5 percent year-over-year rise in first-half earnings to 345 million reais largely because loan defaults fell, the bank's president said.

"Regarding loan defaults, the last three months were the best we had since the beginning of 1995," Itau President Roberto Setubal told Reuters in a telephone interview in which he commented on its first-half results, released Wednesday.
Setubal said he expected the country's second-largest private bank to show improved results in the second half, adding that it would concentrate on its pension and insurance businesses.

Setubal said the decline in loan defaults helped cut the bank's expenses related to loan-loss provisions. Such expenses were reduced to 205 million reais in the first half from 638 million reais in the same period last year.

Brazilian banks, particularly in 1995, suffered from increased corporate and consumer defaults after the government implemented a policy of high interest rates and credit limits in the first stage of its three-year-old Real anti-inflation plan.

High loan defaults prompted most banks to slow their credit businesses and take a more cautious approach to lending, even after the government eased the credit restrictions and moved to cut interest rates.
He said Itau's credit operations grew moderately in the first half of 1997 as the bank continues to emphasize a conservative credit strategy toward retail investors,
The bank's consolidated loan and leasing portfolio grew 16.1 percent to 16.4 billion reais.
Asset-management growth also contributed to Itau's net profit in the January-to-June period, Setubal said.
Itau manages 14.605 billion reais in investment funds and now ranks as the top private investment fund manager, according to Brazil's National Association of Investment Bankers (ANBID).

Setubal also said Itau's takeover of its sister company Itau Seguros in April helped boost the bank's first-half net profit. He said the insurer accounted for 15 million reais of the bank's total profit in the period.
He also said Itau would focus on reorganizing Banco Banerj SA, previously Rio de Janeiro state's bank and Itau's latest bank acquisition.

Itau acquired Banerj in the first privatization auction of a Brazilian state-owned bank in June, paying 178 million reais. The bank was fully acquired with privatization bonds, which are traded at a discount.
Setubal said Itau would invest 50 million reais to modernize Banerj by the beginning of next year.
Banerj has 193 branches, 1.3 million customers and added 2.8 billion reais to Itau's consolidated assets.
Itau ended the first half with 37.8 billion reais in assets, a net worth of 4.098 billion reais and an annualized return on equity of 17.5 percent.
